subject: Private infra: module boundaries, secret handling, and CI 'circuit-breaker' tests
messages:
From: Renee Cole <renee@acmecorp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment preflight: IaC modules + CI checks

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this on. We have a target window in mid-December to stand up our private VPC deployment (Air-gapped variant) using the bundles your team provided. Before we approve the onboarding schedule our security and networking teams need a short preflight review focused on the infrastructure-as-code artifacts and CI gating.

What we'd like to validate:
- Module boundaries: network, cluster, and services should be separable for audits.
- Secret handling: remote state encryption and KMS use, and no static secrets in Helm values.
- CI safety: plan/apply gating, canary stage, and automated rollback/circuit-breaker behavior.
- Network segmentation: explicit ingress/egress controls, bastion requirements, and audit logging hooks.

I attached a small diff with our requested overrides (priv-iac-diff.patch) and a draft values file for Helm (helm-values-acme.yaml). Drive folder with full manifests: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-iac

Can we get a readout by Wednesday (Dec 2)? If we can't meet that timeline we'll need to delay the deployment window.

Thanks,
Renee
Renee Cole
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Corp

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Renee Cole <renee@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment preflight: IaC modules + CI checks

Addendum after a quick pass on the Drive artifacts — high-level findings:

1) Module boundaries
- The terraform tree mixes network and cluster resources in the same module for "core-stack". For audits we should split into: network (VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT, firewall), infra (bastion, monitoring agents), and workloads (k8s cluster + node pools). This will make ownership and drift detection easier.
- Suggest: a lightweight root module that composes clearly named child modules with explicit outputs (vpc_id, shared_subnet_ids, kube_ca_cert).

2) Remote state & locking
- Backend currently configured to use a generic S3 bucket without explicit encryption_by_default. Require: encrypted backend with customer-managed KMS key and a DynamoDB lock table (or equivalent) to prevent parallel applies.

3) Secrets in Helm values
- The supplied helm-values-acme.yaml contains plaintext database_password and app_api_key in top-level values. Replace with references to the KMS-backed secrets store (or sealed-secrets) and document the decryption step in the private deploy runbook.

4) CI patterns
- We must have terraform plan as a PR check. No direct merge to main before plan approval.
- Add a staged canary in the CI pipeline: plan -> apply to canary workspace -> synthetic traffic smoke test -> promote. If smoke test fails, pipeline must auto-roll back and mark the deploy as failed.

5) Ansible idempotency
- Several playbooks use shell tasks that don't check state. Convert to idempotent modules and add a dry-run verification step in CI (ansible --check + parse output).

6) Static IPs and firewall
- Outbound firewall rules are permissive (0.0.0.0/0 for some egress hooks). Need explicit egress allow-lists for known control-plane endpoints.

I'll prepare a proposed patch with module splits and a CI job template.

Laura
Head of Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Renee Cole <renee@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment preflight: IaC modules + CI checks

Couple of implementation notes from the runtime perspective:

- Backend recommendations: use S3 with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) + DynamoDB table for state locking. If Acme requires customer KMS keys we will accept a key ARN during onboarding.

- Provider pinning: pin terraform providers and add a provider-check CI job that fails PRs with non-approved provider versions. This prevents accidental provider upgrades during a deploy.

- Helm charts: add a template check step (helm template | kubeval) in CI to catch broken manifests, and enforce that sensitive values are routed through a secrets templating layer (sealed-secrets or external-secrets).

- Network isolation: require namespace network policies by default. Pod-level egress should be restricted and we should provide an egress-relay pattern for approved external endpoints.

- Circuit-breaker CI job: outline below (to be added to ci-circuit-breaker-testplan.md):
  * After canary apply, run a synthetic traffic job for 10 minutes with health checks and latency thresholds.
  * If >5% errors or 95th percentile latency > configurable threshold, trigger automatic rollback (terraform apply using last-known-good state) and open a PagerDuty incident.
  * Run a post-rollback smoke test to confirm the old version serves.

- Artifact management: helm charts should be packaged and pushed to the customer's private OCI registry; image digests used in helm values, not tags.

I'll attach a quick CI sketch and a list of required inputs (bucket names, KMS ARN, registry) in the follow-up.

-Dev
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment preflight: IaC modules + CI checks

Agree with the above. Operational additions for CI:

- Canary traffic mirroring: pipeline should support traffic mirroring (or small % of real traffic) to the canary using the customer LB if available; otherwise run a synthetic mirror from our test harness.

- Canary gating and kill-switch: implement a pipeline-level kill-switch parameter that can be toggled by on-call. If the canary fails, the job should automatically run terraform to reapply the last-known-good state in the same workspace and mark the PR as failed.

- Signed artifacts: require signed helm chart artifacts (cosign) and verify signatures in CI before apply.

- Monitoring integration: link CI canary results to a temporary alert channel (Slack webhook) that the customer's on-call will confirm before promotion to full rollout.

- Test determinism: include a deterministic smoke test that validates: ingress, egress ACLs, DNS for internal services, and audit-logging is being emitted to the configured endpoint.

I'll add a pipeline snippet to the Drive folder and a sample GitHub Actions workflow for the initial run.

Karthik
Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — good coverage. Summary / action items: 

1) Module split PR (Laura + Dev): move network + infra + cluster into explicit child modules, add outputs for consumption. Target: Dec 4 EOD.
2) Backend hardening (Dev): S3 SSE-KMS + DynamoDB lock table + provider pinning. Target: Dec 3.
3) Secrets migration (Marissa + Customer): replace plaintext Helm secrets with sealed-secrets/external-secrets flow; document decryption runbook. Target: Dec 3.
4) CI: add terraform plan in PR, canary stage with circuit-breaker job, artifact signing check (Karthik). Target: Dec 4 for prototype; Dec 7 for full rollout.
5) Ansible idempotency checks (Laura): convert shell tasks to modules, add --check verification in CI. Target: Dec 6.

Renee — can you confirm the KMS key requirement and whether Acme prefers cross-account key usage? Once we have that I'll attach the PR links and schedule a 30-minute follow-up on Dec 3 to run through the patch set.

Attachments included: priv-iac-diff.patch, ci-circuit-breaker-testplan.md, helm-values-acme.yaml
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-iac
Jira: INFRA-2293

If there are no objections I'll open the module-split PR tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Priyom
